candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record documents both constrictive physiology (ventricular interdependence, septal bounce, thickened pericardium, elevated and equalized filling pressures on catheterization) AND an effusive component (increased IVC size 28 mm with reduced inspiratory collapse, pericardial thickening >40 mm on MRI, PR depressions and ST elevation on ECG suggesting pericardial inflammation/effusion, elevated right atrial pressure). Effusive-constrictive pericarditis requires both elements. C001 captures only the constrictive portion and omits the effusive component, making it a partial parent/component rather than a complete equivalent.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Constrictive pericarditis is a component/subtype of effusive-constrictive pericarditis but omits the effusive component, which is a required part of the benchmark diagnosis

case_quality_flags: Cardiac MRI reports pericardial thickening >40 mm which is anatomically implausible (likely >4 mm intended); does not alter diagnostic classification
